Mythastria style guide

How Mythastria reads and looks, for anyone adding a page, a rule, a map or a picture. It writes down what the table already does (28 October 2026). Where a check found something to fix, or where the GM still has to decide, it says so in a gold box marked Proposed. Three parts: Words, Screens, Art, then a checklist and the professional guides it draws on.

1. Words

Mythastria is written for the GM and the players at the table, in plain words. The rules words are SRD 5.2.1's.

Rules words

  • Game terms are capitalised as the SRD 5.2.1 Rules Glossary has them: Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, Opportunity Attack, Difficult Terrain, Bloodied, Concentration, and the conditions (Prone, Frightened, Stunned...).
  • Abilities in full where a player reads a sentence: "a Dexterity saving throw", "DC 15 Constitution save". Short forms (Dex 14, Str) only in compact stat lines.
  • Numbers the way the SRD writes them: 30 ft, 1d10 + 4, AC 17, DC 15, a level 3 spell slot, 2d10 Fire damage.
  • Only SRD 5.2.1 and Mythastria's own words. No other publisher's names, places, spells or terms in anything Mythastria ships; what a player imports stays theirs (homebrew, local only).

Plain words

  • Say what happened and what to do, never the program's insides (no "op", "snapshot", "revision", "ticket").
  • A refusal gives its reason, and a greyed-out button says why in its hover text:
Goblin 2 is 35 ft away: out of the Scimitar's reach (5 ft).Invalid target. Hero 4's Bonus Action is used this turn.Action not available.
  • Buttons are verbs that name the thing: Cast Shield, End turn, Take over Hero 4, Give Hero 4 back, Hand to the GM, Ask the GM, Answer for them. A question the fight asks ends with a question mark: "Cast Shield? (Reaction)".
  • A player's own screen is the player client, and its turn controls are the player clients' buttons (the GM, 27 October).
  • Hints say what is possible, never which to choose. Suggestions, when they come, are labelled as an opinion.
  • Narration never claims a hit, a miss or damage that the dice did not decide.
  • The Documents page gives each feature in three parts: what it does, how to use it, and its limits, with the date it changed.
Proposed: say GM everywhere Mythastria writes for itself. Today the pages say "the GM" 121 times and "the GM" 41 times (the GM role swap, Restore the party, the Market, "not yet (the GM rules it)" on the Spells page). Quoted SRD text keeps its own wording. The GM decides.

2. Screens

The look

  • Gilded is the default skin (the GM, 22 October: "a touch of elegance"): warm black #100f0c, gold #d9bb78 and parchment-white text #ece2c9; Cormorant Garamond for headings, Inter for text; bevelled buttons and soft shadows. The other skins are Tabletop (the cartoon one), Deep Sea and Parchment (light).
  • Use the colour names, never a colour code, in new pages: --paper text, --muted notes, --brass gold, --panel, --ink, --line, --ok green, --no red. Then every skin works without a change (dist/skins.css).
  • One look for every page: the header, links, panels and buttons come from site.css, skins.css and site.mjs.

Reading and using

  • Text contrast at least 4.5:1 against its background (3:1 for large headings); the edges of boxes you type in, and the focus ring, at least 3:1 (WCAG 2.2).
  • A visible focus ring on everything you can reach with the keyboard: the 2 px gold ring in site.css.
  • Touch targets at least 44 px tall (table-ui.css already does this for buttons and boxes).
  • Motion is short and quiet, and stops for anyone whose device asks for reduced motion (already done in effects.css and the pages).
  • Never a choice made for anyone. Something that pauses the fight is one card near the top of the screen, one at a time, and the GM can always answer for a player (the Reaction question). A choice that can't be taken back says so.

Fixed the same day (--field-edge is the typing boxes' edge colour in every skin):

  1. Parchment's colours: it borrowed the dark skins' green, red and amber, which couldn't be read on parchment (1.4:1, 2.2:1, 1.5:1). It has its own darker ones now, and darker grey notes, gold, rust and sage.
  2. Edges of boxes you type in (and of choosers such as Hints and Limit): at least 3:1 in every skin. Gilded keeps its recessed look (a dark top edge). Panel edges stay faint: they are decoration, not something you use.
  3. The focus ring everywhere: Gilded's typing boxes, the combat tracker's rows and the front page's layout buttons now show the gold ring when reached by the keyboard.
  4. No text under 11 px: the old Training table page's 7-10 px labels are 11 px, as are the Documents page's tags, which also take the skin's own green now.

3. Art

  • Map, 3D world and creatures: "style 1" (the GM, 19 October), the Retro tokens' cartoon drawing: thick ink outlines and two or three flat tones, in muted colours so the bright tokens stand out.
  • Never recolour or restyle a token ("leave the tokens bright coloured").
  • A tabletop miniature, not a photograph: chunky blocks, clean edges, simple solid shapes (a CNC model of a map should one day be possible).
  • Creatures are flat standees on a round base (adjustable in Flavor). The newer SRD token art is a choice in Flavor, never a creature's default.
  • Map walls are at least one 5-ft square: no line walls, a door sits in a doorway square, no floor square on the map's outer edge, and the stone beyond the outer walls fades away.
  • Effects: an ink outline and a flat rim; comic hit stars (bigger for a Critical Hit), a swoosh with puffs for a miss (EFFECTS.md).
  • Only Mythastria's own art and SRD content ship. Art a GM imports stays on their PC.

The palette of the 3D world is dist/world-style.mjs; the skins and their history are in SKINS.md.

Checklist for something new

  1. Rules words as the SRD 5.2.1 Rules Glossary has them; plain words for everything else.
  2. Every refusal and greyed-out button says why.
  3. Colours by name (--paper, --muted...), and it looks right in Gilded and Parchment.
  4. Text at least 4.5:1, typing boxes and the focus ring at least 3:1; the gold focus ring shows.
  5. Buttons at least 44 px tall; it works at a phone's width.
  6. Nothing chosen for anyone; the GM can always answer for a player.
  7. Art: style 1, tokens untouched, thick walls.
  8. Its Documents entry says what, how and the limits, in the same change.

The professional guides behind it

No single guide covers a game like this; these cover its parts.

  • Rules text: the SRD 5.2.1 itself (its Rules Glossary); Wizards of the Coast's D&D style guide for GMs Guild creators (2019, before the 2024 rules); Ray Vallese, Writing With Style; Wolfgang Baur et al., The Complete Kobold Guide to Game Design; the Chicago Manual of Style, which most RPG publishers build on.
  • Screens: WCAG 2.2 (contrast, focus, keyboard); the Xbox Accessibility Guidelines (113: focus that stays visible; 114: knowing what a button does before pressing it); the Game Accessibility Guidelines.
  • Art: studios keep their style guides private; Mythastria's are the GM's own choices above.
